summary: A slide has three content-attempt ordinals per operation attempt: initial authoring, one corrected authoring attempt, and the final simplified author attempt owned by author-stage rescue. Classified overload replay is a separately recorded physical attempt and does not advance the content ordinal.
invariants: Within one operation attempt a slide admits at most three content ordinals, and ordinal three is reserved for the last author attempt.
Every physical provider request is reserved before I/O; a classified overload replay increments physical-attempt accounting without consuming another content ordinal.
Replaying the same content ordinal stays idempotent, while skipping or decreasing an ordinal fails closed.
A stale worker holding an old attempt token cannot advance either content or physical attempt accounting.
Calls spent in earlier operation attempts remain preserved in provider_attempt_total and provider_physical_attempt_total.
A whole-account usage_limit_reached response pauses the deck until its persisted reset boundary instead of failing one slide.
forbidden: Treat overload replay as a fourth content attempt.
Retry a physical request without a durable reservation or beyond the operation deadline.
Replay inside one admission when the provider transport has no confirmed idempotency support.
Treat every generic provider bridge exception as transient.
rationale: The accepted placeholder-authoring design aligns the ledger to the current three-ordinal author budget and reserves the third ordinal for the last author attempt.
Separating content ordinals from physical overload retries preserves the model-repair budget while keeping provider spend bounded and auditable.
Durable quota pause lets the coordinator resume after the provider reset without converting account exhaustion into a slide defect.
